title: Under-covered policy story: defence offsets and the difference between unfulfilled and overdue

verification_claim.text: About 45% of India's defence offset obligations were in default as of December 2025.

definitions: Unfulfilled obligations across ongoing contracts are not automatically the same as overdue or defaulted obligations.
Some obligations in long-running procurement contracts may have future discharge schedules.

evidence.title: Standing Committee Report Summary: Management of Defence Offsets
evidence.evidence_summary: PRS's summary of the Public Accounts Committee report says about 45% of offset obligations remained unfulfilled as of 18 December 2025 and notes contract-management deficiencies.

evidence.title: Pending Rs 42,000-Crore Defence Offsets Trigger Scrutiny, Expert Says Concerns May Be Overstated
evidence.evidence_summary: The article reports expert caution that the 45% figure covers ongoing obligations, some of which were not yet due; it says claims had been submitted against more than 82% of obligations that had actually fallen due by December 2025.

evidence.title: Unstarred Question No. 2823 — Offset Contracts
evidence.evidence_summary: An earlier official parliamentary answer separately reported total offset-contract value, claims submitted, and offset amounts due, illustrating that total obligations and amounts actually due are distinct categories.

research_summary: The Public Accounts Committee summary supports the statement that roughly 45% of offset obligations remained unfulfilled in late 2025. However, describing the entire 45% as 'in default' overstates what that figure means because ongoing obligations can include future scheduled discharge. Reporting on the PAC data indicates that a much larger share of obligations that had actually fallen due already had claims submitted. The useful story is the distinction between unfulfilled total obligations and overdue/defaulted obligations.

locked_claims.text: The PAC summary said about 45% of defence offset obligations remained unfulfilled as of December 2025.
Unfulfilled total obligations are not necessarily equivalent to overdue/defaulted obligations.
The PAC also identified contract-management and verification deficiencies.

material_caveats: The 45% figure refers to unfulfilled obligations across ongoing offset contracts, not necessarily obligations already overdue.
The system should distinguish total outstanding obligations from obligations that had fallen due.
prohibited_claims: 45% of defence offset obligations had definitively defaulted.
45% of offset obligations were written off.
All unfulfilled obligations had already reached their contractual due date.
